text: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Hobart. Which public liability lawyers are best?

sections.text:
For a Hobart shopping-centre slip-and-fall, compare **Tasmanian public-liability specialists** rather than choosing solely by advertising. Strong options to contact include:

- **Murdoch Clarke Lawyers** — Hobart firm with a dedicated personal-injury and public-liability practice; phone **(03) 6235 9303**.[5]
- **Jovanovic Lawyers** — Hobart personal-injury practice offering an initial discussion; phone **(03) 6223 3344**.[4]
- **Slater and Gordon** — national firm with a Hobart public-liability team and experience with shopping and slip-and-fall claims.[2][6]
- **Lawyers, Doctors & Health (LDH)** — advertises Hobart public-liability and slip-and-fall claims on a no-win-no-fee basis, subject to its costs agreement.[1][3]
- **Maurice Blackburn** — national personal-injury firm handling injuries in public places.[10]

**Best shortlist:** obtain free initial consultations from Murdoch Clarke, Jovanovic, and either Slater and Gordon or LDH. Ask each lawyer about relevant shopping-centre cases, their fee percentage and disbursements, likely claim value, and whether they act under a genuine “no win, no fee” agreement.

Before contacting anyone:

- Photograph the exact hazard, your injuries, clothing and footwear.
- Report the fall to centre management and request an incident report.
- Obtain names and contact details of witnesses.
- Keep medical records, receipts and time-off-work evidence.
- Avoid giving a recorded statement or accepting a settlement before legal advice.

A public-liability claim generally depends on proving that the shopping centre or another responsible party failed to take reasonable care—not merely that a fall occurred. In Australia, the limitation period can be as short as three years for this type of claim, so obtain advice promptly.[6]
